title: Depression, not drinking, and no warning from Basie
summary: Edison says he never drank, was afraid, was married, and recounts joining Basie around 21 in late 1937.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Did you drink during that period?
Never drank. Not to excess. Took a drink every now and then.
Like you did last night. An occasional one.

Yeah. I never did drink. Never had no desire for it, you know. And I was really -- I was afraid. I didn't know where I was going to get any money from and what I was going to do. I was really depressed.
Yes. Yes, I was married then.
So you had to think of that, too.

Yeah. Yeah. Well, I joined Basie -- not quite at 22. I joined Basie when I was around 21. Around 21, because it was just after my 21st birthday. 21st, because I joined him in the latter part of '37, just before Christmas. And then Herschel died right after I got with the band, in '38, see.* But it's really -- you know, when you've been dependent on somebody for years, never had to worry about it, and all of a sudden -- then you don't even know it. There was no preparation for it. You know, he didn't say, "Well, this is it, you know. You go your way and I'll go mine because it's come to the point where I just can't afford a big band anymore."
I guess sort of half truths like that, he didn't --
I don't know. Nobody knows what he was thinking of. Well, it happened for the best because it made me realize that I've got to look out for myself, you know.
Yes. Because the band could have -- well, it did collapse.

Yeah, the smaller one. And I went with Jazz at the Philharmonic and I played with everybody around New York. I was making records. I recorded quite a bit. And I was just doing studio work around New York.
